_comment: LLM-MAINTAINED MODULE MAP for @argo/desktop. Single source of truth for module boundaries; dependency-cruiser.cjs turns it into lint rules mechanically — edit this map, never the generated rules. Refresh when the src/ structure changes. Managed by the setup-module-boundaries skill.

modules.name: shared
modules.comment: Cross-process contract: the Session state list and the union derived from it, the delivery facts main observes, the event vocabulary, projected-state types, IPC channel names, the pure projection reducer, and the lifecycle derivation (session facts → delivery render state). Types, frozen constants and pure functions only — no I/O, no framework. `SessionView` carries facts, never a rendered state, so grading stays on the renderer's side of the bridge. Imported by all three processes (renderer files reach it through the `@shared` alias), imports none of them.

modules.name: main
modules.comment: Electron main process. Its internals are private; the app is wired only from its own entry.

modules.name: preload
modules.comment: The context-bridge. Loaded by Electron via file path, not imported — nothing should import its internals.

modules.name: renderer
modules.comment: The UI (browser context). Talks to main only through the window bridge, never by import.

modules.name: renderer-shared
modules.comment: The renderer's shared leaf (feature-sliced `shared/`): the framework-primitive kit (`components/ui` + its icons) that every slice composes, and the status presentation vocabulary (`shared/status`: the Roster status word/icon and the `deliveryState` composition over the `@shared` lifecycle derivation). That folder was named `shared/delivery` until #284 renamed it, because what it holds is the status word/tone vocabulary every room reads and the old name promised a Delivery coupling the room slices must not have. A building block imported by two or more domains lives here, so every domain may import it and it imports no domain in return. External code reaches it only through the three barrels; its internals are private.

modules.name: cockpit
modules.comment: The composition root's WIRING: the hooks that read the Zustand store and the preload bridge and assemble each slice's props, plus the stage that picks the active room's component. Slices are pure Views (rules/ui-components.md, container/View: 'the View never imports data access'), so this is the one place on the renderer side where the store and the bridge are read — which is why this wiring cannot live inside `shell/` even though most of it serves the shell. It may import every slice's public entry; no slice may import it, so the dependency runs root → slice and never back. Its own files stay behind `cockpit/index.ts`, which `App.tsx` is the only caller of.

modules.name: shell
modules.comment: The shell slice (cockpit-spec.md §11.2, inventory in docs/designs/cockpit-ui-inventory.md): the project strip, the one merged floating top bar and its four regions (orb seat, connection chip, room tabs, global git group), the ⌘K palette, the keymap, the empty first-run seam, the connect/Project-Settings panel, spawn and navigation. Chrome renders in all three rooms or it is not chrome. A peer of the room slices, never their parent. The renderer root composes shell + active room, so the shell reaches into no room and no room reaches into it.

modules.name: rooms-sessions
modules.comment: The Sessions room (⌘1, home): the roster rail and the session interior: header, the two-pane Activity surface, Delivery, and the always-on Dock. On the locked runtime vocabulary (Agent · Subagent · Turn · Tool Call · Plan · Workspace · Compaction · Usage), not the retired Run/Phase/Actor names. Composed by the renderer root through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another slice.

modules.name: rooms-work
modules.comment: The Work room (⌘2): the list rail (Next-up hero over a priority hierarchy), the generic node tree where type is a property rather than a schema, and the two-pane ticket detail. Renders the Work Item provider's own status word verbatim; the canonical bucket is ranking/filtering only. Composed by the renderer root through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another slice.

modules.name: rooms-code
modules.comment: The Code room (⌘3), session-independent: the file explorer over the primary checkout, name-or-content search, the lightweight editable editor, the scratch terminal attached to no agent, and the degraded file states. Composed by the renderer root through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another slice.

modules.name: roster
modules.comment: RETIRED (#157; disposition in docs/designs/cockpit-ui-inventory.md). The Roster Panel (CONTEXT.md region): the session roster column and its rows. A feature slice — owns its `components/` and, as they arrive, its hooks/store/types. Composed by the screen through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another domain.

modules.name: activity
modules.comment: RETIRED (#157; disposition in docs/designs/cockpit-ui-inventory.md). The Activity Panel (CONTEXT.md region; supersedes ADR-0009's `story/`): the Background Tasks roster — Runs, Agents, phases. A feature slice composed by the screen through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another domain.

modules.name: delivery
modules.comment: RETIRED (#157; disposition in docs/designs/cockpit-ui-inventory.md). The Delivery Panel (CONTEXT.md region; supersedes ADR-0009's `work/`): the Delivery lifecycle and node drawers — DeliveryLifecycle + NodeDrawer, the CI card molecules, the LifecycleNode state→icon/tone vocabulary. Pure Views over the pre-derived `LifecycleModel` from `@shared`. A feature slice composed by the screen through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another domain.

modules.name: console
modules.comment: RETIRED (#157; disposition in docs/designs/cockpit-ui-inventory.md). The Console Panel (CONTEXT.md region, cockpit-matrix.md R13): the ONE monospace surface, its channel strip and channel body, plus the channel vocabulary and the three derivations over it (`captureLabel`, `resolveActiveChannel`, `feedLines`). A feature slice composed by the screen through its barrel; its internals are private and it never reaches into another domain.

layers._comment: Two isolations. (1) Electron process isolation: the three processes must never import each other — the only channels are the preload bridge (renderer↔main) and Electron's own preload wiring (main→preload by path). All three may import `shared` (the cross-process type/pure-function contract); `shared` imports none of them. (2) Renderer feature-slice isolation, unchanged in kind by the #157 redesign and now applied to the shell + room slices as well: a slice must not reach into another slice's internals (slices ⊥ slices, so shell ⊥ rooms and room ⊥ room); every slice may import `renderer-shared`; `renderer-shared` is a leaf that imports no slice. The shell is a PEER of the rooms, not their parent: the renderer root composes shell + active room outside every slice, exactly as `SessionScreen` composes the retired panel domains today. The four remaining retired domains keep their rules until their last file moves; `concierge` left in #284 (ADR-0019). (3) The composition root's wiring (`cockpit`) is the only renderer code that reads the store or the bridge, and the dependency runs one way: it imports slices, no slice imports it.

placement._comment: WHERE FILES MAY LIVE, as opposed to what they may import. dependency-cruiser only sees edges, so a feature's own file parked at the app root — or a one-caller helper parked in the shared tier — passes every boundary rule while sitting in the wrong folder. These two blocks compile into the gates `scripts/composition-root-check.mjs` and `scripts/earned-shared-check.mjs` (run by `bun run quality`), which is what turns the prose in rules/file-structure.md into arithmetic. Each exemption is labelled KIND (the rule does not apply to that category) or RATCHET (debt; the list may only shrink), the same convention as biome.jsonc and file-length-exempt.txt.

compositionRoot.comment: The renderer root holds only what belongs to no module: the bootstrap, the container that wires the slices, and its View. Slice-owned files and slice-serving wiring both have homes — `<slice>/` and `cockpit/` — so a file loose here is a file that skipped the decision.

allow.main.tsx: KIND — the bootstrap: mounts App into the DOM. Belongs to no module by definition.
allow.env.d.ts: KIND — ambient renderer types (the preload bridge shape, the csstype augmentation). Not a module's code.
allow.App.tsx: KIND — the container (rules/ui-components.md): reads the store through `cockpit/` and renders the root View. The one file allowed to know both.
allow.CockpitScreenView.tsx: KIND — the root View: props in, JSX out, composing shell + active room. Its whole job is to sit outside every slice.
allow.CockpitScreenView.stories.tsx: KIND — the root View's story, which ui-components.md makes mandatory. Lives beside its View.

ratchet.SessionScreen.tsx: RATCHET — pre-#264 screen for the retired panel domains; leaves when rooms-sessions lands (#265).
ratchet.SessionScreen.stories.tsx: RATCHET — story for the above; goes with it.
ratchet.SessionHeader.tsx: RATCHET — session-interior component at the root; belongs in rooms-sessions (#265).
ratchet.SessionHeader.stories.tsx: RATCHET — story for the above; goes with it.
ratchet.sessionScreenModel.ts: RATCHET — the retired screen's derivation; belongs in rooms-sessions (#265).
ratchet.sessionScreenModel.test.ts: RATCHET — test for the above; goes with it.
ratchet.useSpineLayout.ts: RATCHET — the retired screen's layout hook; belongs in rooms-sessions (#265).
ratchet.useSpineLayout.test.ts: RATCHET — test for the above; goes with it.
ratchet.WorkspaceIdentity.tsx: RATCHET — session-interior component at the root; belongs in rooms-sessions (#265).
ratchet.WorkspaceIdentity.stories.tsx: RATCHET — story for the above; goes with it.
ratchet.WorkspaceIdentity.test.ts: RATCHET — test for the above; goes with it.
ratchet.sessionStore.ts: RATCHET — the projected-state store. Read only by `cockpit/`, so it wants to move in there; kept at the root this pass to hold the diff to structure.
ratchet.sessionStore.test.ts: RATCHET — test for the above; goes with it.

earnedShared.comment: A symbol earns the shared tier on its THIRD caller (rules/file-structure.md), but the gate enforces the FLOOR at two: the rule calls two callers 'either — copy it, or hoist', so only a single-caller symbol is unambiguously misplaced and arithmetic must not adjudicate a judgement call. Counted per symbol across modules, because everything leaves the tier through a barrel and a file-level graph would show every module depending on every leaf behind it.
earnedShared.ratchet_: Each entry below is a symbol in the domain-aware tier with one caller left; they leave when the retired panel domains do (#284). The tier itself is now `shared/status`; #284 renamed it.
earnedShared._exclude_comment: KIND — the framework-primitive kit (`components/ui`, its icons, the docs blocks). file-structure.md earns the generic tier by CATEGORY, not by caller count: these would stand alone as a published package, so a vendored Radix wrapper or an icon belongs to the kit from its first caller. Counting callers here would flag 50 icons and demand they be scattered into the slices that happen to use one each.

ratchet.isHotHeadState: RATCHET — only `delivery` reads it; moves in with the lifecycle rail (#265).
ratchet.lifecycleIsHot: RATCHET — only `roster` reads it; moves in with the roster rail (#265).
ratchet.RosterIcon: RATCHET — the status-icon type, read only by `delivery` today; earns the tier again once a second room renders a status icon.

kindFolders.comment: Folders named for what files ARE rather than what they're for. `lib/` is absent deliberately: rules/file-structure.md names it as the one sanctioned shared tier. `components/` is absent because a slice's `components/` holds one feature's components, which is the opposite of a junk drawer.

ratchet.src/renderer/src/hooks: RATCHET — pre-#264 kind-folder holding one generic hook (`useDisclosure`). Its callers decide its home: one caller means it moves in beside it, three means it earns `lib/`.
